title: Two crypto trend systems, walk-forward tested, every year positive. Tell me why this is wrong.
author: kingsbichon
selftext:
I built two automated strategies that trade BTC and ETH. Both follow trends, but they get in at different moments, so they rarely win or lose at the same time. I'd rather not post the rules publicly, but I'm happy to share them in PM if you want to dig in properly.



How I tested it (trying not to fool myself)



\- I never tested on data the strategy had already been tuned on. Every 3 months, the settings are chosen using the previous 12 months, then run on the next 3 months blind. I only count those blind results.

\- Trading fees, slippage and funding are all deducted.

\- Every trade risks 1% of the account. Results are in "R", where 1 R = 1% of the account.

\- I built it on 2021-2026 data. Then I ran it on 2018-2020, which it had never seen.



Results



\- 2022-2026, both strategies together: +438 R, worst drawdown about -20 R, worst year still +10 R.

\- 2018-2020, the never-seen years: +229 R, worst drawdown -16 R.

\- No losing year in nine years.



Versus buy and hold



\- 2022-2026: the main strategy alone made about +1,250% with a -17% max drawdown. Holding BTC made +62% with a -67% drawdown. Holding ETH lost money.

\- It's not magic though. In 2021 and 2024 buy and hold beat it badly. The bots earn in explosive breakout years and sit flat in slow grinding bull markets and in bear markets.

\- Simulation of $300 to start plus $300 a month from Aug 2018 ($29k deposited total): the two bots end at about $519k with a -22% worst drawdown. The same deposits into BTC end at about $132k with a -74% drawdown.



What worries me



1. Only 29% of trades win. A few huge winners pay for everything. Take away the top 5 trades and the main strategy is basically break-even.

2. Those huge winners happened when the market was very quiet, so the position size was 4-6x the account. It needs 10x leverage to be possible at all.

3. One strategy uses limit orders. The backtest assumes they always get filled when price touches them. Real life may be worse.

4. The $519k figure compounds two strategies on one account and most of it comes from one breakout in Aug 2026. Treat it as an illustration, not a forecast.



Does the testing method look sound to you? What else would you check before trusting this? I'm going to paper trade it next. PM me if you want the details

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Your walk-forward protects the parameters, not the choice to trade trends on crypto at all. You picked a trend system in 2026 already knowing 2018-2020 held huge directional moves, so the holdout tests the settings honestly but cannot test the decision you made before the code existed.

Second thing: you say both bots sit flat in slow grinding markets. Then no losing year in nine really means nine years never contained a long enough grind. What is the worst flat stretch in months, rather than the worst drawdown in R?

Dormant Breakout code:

    """DormantBreakout: enter when a quiet market (low ADX) closes beyond its 20-bar range in the direction of
    the 200-bar trend. Fixed ATR stop, chandelier trail, add units as the trade climbs. Loses a little often,
    wins a lot rarely (walk-forward win rate ~29%, average win ~7R).
    
    
    The live bot and the backtester both call `generate_signals`; the exit/pyramid rules live in ExitConfig.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    
    
    from okxbot.strategies.base import Strategy, StrategyParams, add_indicators, finalize
    
    
    
    def generate_signals(df: pd.DataFrame, p: StrategyParams) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """`signal` = +1 / -1 on the bar whose close breaks the previous `donchian_period` bars' extreme.
        The engine enters at the next open. With `intrabar_entry` the fill is at the level on the breakout bar."""
        out = add_indicators(df, p)
        upper = out["high"].shift(1).rolling(p.donchian_period).max()
        lower = out["low"].shift(1).rolling(p.donchian_period).min()
        out["donchian_upper"], out["donchian_lower"] = upper, lower
        if p.intrabar_entry:
            long_trig = out["high"] > upper
            short_trig = out["low"] < lower
            # Fill at the level, or at the open if the bar gapped through it.
            out["entry_price"] = np.where(long_trig, np.maximum(out["open"], upper),
                                          np.where(short_trig, np.minimum(out["open"], lower), np.nan))
            # Everything else is evaluated on the previous (closed) bar.
            for col in ("ema", "rsi", "atr", "adx", "regime", "ema_slope", "atr_pct"):
                if col in out:
                    out[col] = out[col].shift(1)
            out["close_ref"] = out["close"].shift(1)
        else:
            long_trig = out["close"] > upper
            short_trig = out["close"] < lower
        return finalize(out, long_trig, short_trig, p, intrabar=p.intrabar_entry)
    
    
    
    STRATEGY = Strategy("dormant_breakout",
                        "20-bar Donchian breakout with the EMA200 trend, only when ADX < 25; ATR stop, chandelier trail, pyramid",
                        generate_signals, entry_modes=("donchian",))

Dormant Breakout config:

    # v13 (2026-09-01) = DormantBreakout, the LIVE strategy. v11 + ADX ceiling (skip breakouts when ADX(14) > 25: trend already old). Ceiling is also in the WF grid.
    instruments:
      - symbol: BTC/USD
        okx_inst_id: BTC-USDT-SWAP
        kind: crypto
      - symbol: ETH/USD
        okx_inst_id: ETH-USDT-SWAP
        kind: crypto
    
    
    data:
      timeframe: 4h
      start: "2021-01-01"
      cache_dir: data/cache
    
    
    strategy:
      name: dormant_breakout
      entry_mode: donchian
      donchian_period: 20
      ema_period: 200
      use_ema_filter: true
      regime_filter: false
      regime_ema_period: 50
      regime_slope_bars: 5
      rsi_period: 14
      rsi_threshold: 45
      stoch_period: 14
      stoch_k: 3
      stoch_d: 3
      stoch_oversold: 20
      structure_entry: false
      confirm_bars: 3
      stop_mode: atr
      swing_lookback: 5
      min_stop_atr: 1.0
      adx_max: 25
      atr_period: 14
      atr_mult: 2.0
      reward_ratio: 3.0
      allow_long: true
      allow_short: true
    
    
    exit:
      mode: trail
      trail_atr: 3.0
      trail_after_r: 1.0
      use_target: false
      pyramid_levels: [2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0]
      pyramid_unit: 1.0
      partial_r: 1.5
      partial_fraction: 0.5
    
    
    costs:
      fee_pct: 0.0005
      slippage_pct: 0.0002
    
    
    risk:
      risk_per_trade: 0.01
      initial_equity: 10000
    
    
    optimize:
      min_trades: 20
      grid:                        # walk-forward re-selects these per window
        donchian_period: [20, 30, 55]
        atr_mult: [2.0, 2.5]
        adx_max: [0, 25, 30]
    
    
    walk_forward:
      train_months: 12
      test_months: 3
      step_months: 3

Catch the move code:

    """CatchTheMove: in a strong trend, a limit order rests just beyond a long moving average to catch the instant
    bounce when a flush hits the line.
    
    
    Long: the close was >= `catch_dist_atr` ATR above the line within the last `catch_window` bars and the last close is
    still above it. The order for the coming bar sits at line - `catch_offset_atr` ATR (both taken from the last closed
    bar, so nothing is known early). It fills if the bar's low reaches it (`fill_pass_atr` = 0: on touch). Stop =
    `atr_mult` ATR below the fill. Exit: chandelier trail after +1R plus `exit.max_bars_losing` (close if not in profit
    after N bars: the bounce is supposed to be immediate). Shorts mirror in a downtrend.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    
    
    from okxbot.indicators import moving_average, rsi
    from okxbot.strategies.base import Strategy, StrategyParams, add_indicators, finalize
    
    
    
    def htf_context(htf: pd.DataFrame, p: StrategyParams) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Line, ATR, ADX and the trend flags on higher-timeframe bars (one row per closed bar). Used by the backtest
        (after resampling) and by the live bot (on 4h candles from the exchange), so both see the same numbers."""
        h = add_indicators(htf, p)
        h["line"] = moving_average(h["close"], p.line_period, p.line_type)
        dist = (h["close"] - h["line"]) / h["atr"]
        h["up_trend"] = (dist.rolling(p.catch_window).max() >= p.catch_dist_atr) & (h["close"] > h["line"])
        h["down_trend"] = (dist.rolling(p.catch_window).min() <= -p.catch_dist_atr) & (h["close"] < h["line"])
        return h
    
    
    
    def approach_ok(fine: pd.DataFrame, p: StrategyParams, side: int, atr: float) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """The v3.2 'dip, not crash' filters on the last CLOSED fine bar, for a prospective trade in `side`.
        Returns (ok, plain-English reason)."""
        bars_4h = max(1, int(pd.Timedelta("4h") / (fine.index[1] - fine.index[0])))
        c = fine["close"]
        if p.max_flush_atr > 0 and len(c) > bars_4h:
            move = side * (c.iloc[-1] - c.iloc[-1 - bars_4h]) / atr
            if move < -p.max_flush_atr:
                return False, f"price moved {move:+.1f} ATR against the trend over the last 4h (crash, not dip; limit {p.max_flush_atr})"
        if p.min_touch_rsi > 0:
            r = float(rsi(c, 14).iloc[-1])
            r_signed = r if side == 1 else 100 - r
            if r_signed < p.min_touch_rsi:
                return False, f"15m RSI {r:.0f} too stretched (needs {'>=' if side == 1 else '<='} {p.min_touch_rsi if side == 1 else 100 - p.min_touch_rsi:.0f})"
        return True, "approach is orderly"
    
    
    
    def _higher_tf_context(df: pd.DataFrame, p: StrategyParams) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Backtest path: resample the fine bars to `line_timeframe`, compute the context, map it back with no lookahead.
        A higher-timeframe bar covering [t, t+tf) becomes known at t+tf, so its values apply to fine bars from t+tf on."""
        tf = p.line_timeframe
        htf = df.resample(tf, label="left", closed="left").agg({"open": "first", "high": "max", "low": "min", "close": "last"}).dropna()
        h = htf_context(htf, p)
        cols = ["line", "atr", "up_trend", "down_trend"] + (["adx"] if "adx" in h else []) + (["ema"] if "ema" in h else [])
        known = h[cols].copy()
        known.index = known.index + pd.tseries.frequencies.to_offset(tf)
        return known.reindex(df.index, method="ffill")
    
    
    
    def generate_signals(df: pd.DataFrame, p: StrategyParams) -> pd.DataFrame:
        out = add_indicators(df, p)
        if p.line_timeframe:
            ctx = _higher_tf_context(df, p)
            out["line"] = ctx["line"]
            for col in ("atr", "adx", "ema"):
                if col in ctx:
                    out[col] = ctx[col]                    # stops, filters and the trail use the higher-timeframe values
            line_prev, atr_prev, close_prev = ctx["line"], ctx["atr"], out["close"].shift(1)
            up_trend, down_trend = ctx["up_trend"].fillna(False).astype(bool), ctx["down_trend"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
            line = ctx["line"]
        else:
            line = moving_average(out["close"], p.line_period, p.line_type)
            out["line"] = line
            # everything the order is built from is known at the previous close
            line_prev, atr_prev, close_prev = line.shift(1), out["atr"].shift(1), out["close"].shift(1)
            dist_prev = ((out["close"] - line) / out["atr"]).shift(1)
            up_trend = (dist_prev.rolling(p.catch_window).max() >= p.catch_dist_atr) & (close_prev > line_prev)
            down_trend = (dist_prev.rolling(p.catch_window).min() <= -p.catch_dist_atr) & (close_prev < line_prev)
        buy_px = line_prev - p.catch_offset_atr * atr_prev
        sell_px = line_prev + p.catch_offset_atr * atr_prev
        out["order_long"], out["order_short"] = buy_px, sell_px
        out["up_trend"], out["down_trend"] = up_trend.fillna(False).astype(bool), down_trend.fillna(False).astype(bool)
        pass_ = p.fill_pass_atr * atr_prev
        long_trig = up_trend & (out["low"] <= buy_px - pass_)
        short_trig = down_trend & (out["high"] >= sell_px + pass_)
        # ---- quality filters on the approach into the line (all from the previous bar: known before the touch) ----
        if p.max_vol_ratio > 0 and "volume" in out:
            vr = (out["volume"] / out["volume"].rolling(p.vol_window).mean()).shift(1)
            out["vol_ratio"] = vr
            ok = (vr <= p.max_vol_ratio).fillna(False)
            long_trig &= ok
            short_trig &= ok
        if p.max_flush_atr > 0:
            bars_4h = max(1, int(pd.Timedelta("4h") / (out.index[1] - out.index[0])))
            move = (out["close"].shift(1) - out["close"].shift(1 + bars_4h)) / atr_prev
            long_trig &= (move >= -p.max_flush_atr).fillna(False)
            short_trig &= (move <= p.max_flush_atr).fillna(False)
        if p.min_touch_rsi > 0:
            r = rsi(out["close"], 14).shift(1)
            long_trig &= (r >= p.min_touch_rsi).fillna(False)
            short_trig &= (r <= 100 - p.min_touch_rsi).fillna(False)
        if p.catch_entry == "confirm":
            # no fill ambiguity: the bar touched the order AND closed back beyond the line; enter at the next open
            long_trig &= out["close"] > line
            short_trig &= out["close"] < line
            return finalize(out, long_trig.fillna(False), short_trig.fillna(False), p)
        # a gap through the order fills at the open
        out["entry_price"] = np.where(long_trig, np.minimum(out["open"], buy_px),
                                      np.where(short_trig, np.maximum(out["open"], sell_px), np.nan))
        # indicators for the stop/filters are the previous bar's (the bar is not closed when the order fills)
        if not p.line_timeframe:
            for col in ("ema", "atr", "adx", "regime", "ema_slope", "atr_pct"):
                if col in out:
                    out[col] = out[col].shift(1)
        out["close_ref"] = close_prev
        return finalize(out, long_trig.fillna(False), short_trig.fillna(False), p, intrabar=True)
    
    
    
    STRATEGY = Strategy("catch_the_move", "Order just beyond a long EMA (EMA100 on 4h) in a strong trend; catches the bounce after a flush",
                        generate_signals)

    # v3.3 (2026-09-02), from v3.2: stop 1.25 ATR instead of 1.5 (winners rarely dip below -0.75R; grid lets WF pick 1.0/1.25/1.5).
    extends: v3.2_dip_not_crash.yaml
    strategy:
      atr_mult: 1.25
    optimize:
      grid:
        catch_window: [20, 40]
        adx_max: [0, 25]
        atr_mult: [1.0, 1.25, 1.5]
